text:
OpenAI open-sourced the Codex harness this week and most coverage described it as a CLI update. It is not.

What changed: the harness -- the runtime that actually runs OpenAI's own coding agent -- was released under Apache 2.0, along with the Codex CLI, an SDK and an app-server for embedding persistent agents in your own product.

What it actually does: it is the loop around the model, not the model. Task decomposition, tool and shell execution, memory that survives across sessions and disconnects, approval checkpoints, sandbox policy, and streamed progress events. Everything you were going to write yourself between the API call and a working agent.

Why builders should care: OpenAI reports the harness took GPT-5.6 Sol on ARC-AGI-3 from 13.3% to 38.3% and cut token use roughly 6x. Same weights. The gain came from the scaffolding. Which means the scaffolding was never the boring part -- it was most of the result, and it just stopped being yours to invent.

Try this this week: pick one repetitive job you already do by hand -- updating a changelog, triaging an inbox folder, regenerating a config -- and wrap it in the harness with an approval step in the middle. One task. Keep the human checkpoint. See what it costs you in tokens versus doing it in a chat window.

The bigger signal: when the agent loop becomes a dependency, nobody wins by having one. The advantage moves to what you point it at, what context you feed it, and where you put the human. The engine is commodity. The workflow is not.

Save this before your next build.

text:
Slack just turned AI coding into a group chat, and the best feature in it is the one that says no.

Slack Code launched this month. You tag an agent in a conversation -- Claude Code, Devin, Copilot -- and it opens a code channel with a plan tab, a live diff tab and a preview. Engineers and non-engineers watch the same work happen.

Nothing ships until a human in that channel approves it. Then the channel archives itself as a record of who asked, what it did, and who said yes.

We run the same shape. Every post on this account is written overnight by an agent and sits in a pull request until a person merges it.

On Tech Thursday, Gabe Coleman showed his version -- the whole batch schedules itself the night before, and he can still move any of it by hand.

The agent does the work. The gate is the job.

ChatGPT can read your text messages now. The install screen is the part worth reading.

OpenAI shipped an Apple Messages plugin for Mac on August 20. It searches your iMessage history, summarizes long threads, drafts replies in your tone, and sends them once you approve. It runs locally on Apple silicon.

That is not a scare story. That is the actual skill.

AI fluency was never just knowing which model to pick. It is knowing exactly what you handed over to get the convenience.

Read the permission screen. Then decide.

text:
Your AI stops looking like you around image four. Everybody blames the model. It is a filing problem.

On Tech Thursday, Gabe Coleman said it out loud -- he uploads his headshot, and a few generations later it has drifted into a stranger wearing his outfit. Then he showed the workflow he uses to stop it, and none of it is clever.

Ask for drafts before you ask for the final. Different formats, same style, four directions -- then you pick one. You are choosing, not describing.

Paste the winner back in. Take the one image that worked, feed it in as the reference, and ask for a matched set built from it. That is how you get four frames that look like one campaign instead of four separate guesses.

Load the project sources. Not just a folder with a name on it -- the headshot, the logo, the colors, the old flyers you already liked. It reaches for those before it invents something.

And this was not the two hundred dollar tier. Gabe built the whole set on the standard plan, and project folders exist on the free one. His words: even the free version has this.

Consistent brands are not prompting better. They are filing better.

Comment BUILD and I'll send you the workflow map.
